title_as_printed: Comparison of physical measurements of oxygen solubility with chemical determination (ml/l. from an atmosphere of 20.94 % O2, 100 % relative humidity).
pressure_note: equilibration with pure oxygen at atmospheric pressure (physical gasometric method of Part I, Bunsen coefficient basis, 760 Torr gas pressure), values then expressed as ml/l from air of 20.94 % O2 and 100 % RH

value.what: converted by authors from the measured Bunsen coefficient of pure O2 to air-saturation basis

value2.col: Chemical measurements: Present work smooth curve
value2.what: smoothed Table 2 value of this paper (derived)

composition.other_species: sea water identified by chlorinity (permil), 0.000 = distilled water; use chlorinity x 1.80655 for salinity (stated in the text)

conversion_needs: chlorinity to salinity: S = Cl x 1.80655 (paper's own relation)
ml/l to mole fraction needs STP molar volume and water density
notes: Physical (pure-O2 gasometric) determinations of Part I converted to the air basis; the 0.000 chlorinity rows are distilled water. The chlorinity-based composition basis has no builder code yet; salinity may be computed as chlorinity x 1.80655. Rows are in the printed order (not temperature-sorted).
volume_basis_evidence: Murray and Riley 1969 (O2): solubility in ml/l; the paper does not say whether the litre is of seawater or of water.

row_duplicate_of.reason: pure-water rows at 13.60, 25.72 and 28.31 C are the same measurements as Table 2 of Murray and Riley 1969 (N2/O2 Bunsen, doi 10.1016/0011-7471(69)90020-5) in other units (audit, 2026-10-02)
